body.title: Manage saved and temporary data connections
body.problem: Users need a discoverable way to maintain saved analysis sources and use one-off sources with an explicit lifetime. They need to know whether a change was saved and is available for analysis, retain control of credentials, and clean up registrations without deleting source data. This Epic defines those required outcomes; current implementation observations and gaps are recorded separately in its grounding evidence.

summary.prose: Manage saved and temporary data connections from Settings without editing JSON. Required outcomes include draft tests, credential control, truthful save results, and safe removal. This is a delivery definition; acceptance checks remain pending implementation. Product scope is [[c1]], with runtime driver selection [[c9]] and an illustrative mock [[c8]].

nonGoals.text: New drivers, automatic config discovery, ontology generation, team-shared credentials
nonGoals.rationale: Required release boundary in [[c12]]: keep this release focused on connection management.

assumptions.text: The CM01-CM08 PRD supplies the required product outcomes. The fictional mock does not verify production acceptance.
External IDE integration is a delivery dependency to verify during HLD; current pane reuse and compatibility are not assumed established by this definition.

constraints.text: Required delivery invariant (not an existing implementation guarantee): Daemon owns persistence and secrets; clients use IPC and never receive stored secret values.

Required delivery invariant (not an existing implementation guarantee): Read failures and stale mutations preserve existing registry and credentials; uncertain responses reconcile idempotently. Read-failure preservation also follows CM06 [[c10]].
Required delivery invariant (not an existing implementation guarantee): Temporary scope is workbench-session and repository isolated, memory-only, and expires at session end or daemon restart.
Required delivery invariant (not an existing implementation guarantee): Removal never deletes source files or database data and refuses busy connections.
Required delivery invariant (not an existing implementation guarantee): Preserve existing IPC clients through an explicit compatibility strategy and synchronize the separate IDE contract.

stories.title: Manage saved endpoints and credentials without losing configuration
stories.userValue: Safely maintain saved sources. These are proposed delivery acceptance criteria, to be validated by this Story’s build; they do not assert existing production support.

functionalRequirements.statement: Required outcome: Manage saved endpoints and credentials without losing configuration.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A registered repository and supported driver
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user adds or edits a saved connection
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Create rejects duplicate IDs, edit fixes ID/driver, non-secret fields populate, unknown supported fields survive, and Keep/Replace/Clear credentials apply explicitly; cancel changes nothing

acceptanceCriteria.given: Concurrent changes or an unreadable registry
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Stale edits cannot overwrite or recreate deleted entries; simultaneous creates yield one success; failed reads and mutations preserve registry and credentials
Required result: Persistence, activation and refresh are separate; failed activation/refresh retries do not repeat create; lost responses reconcile the same operation before further mutation

stories.title: Test the current draft safely and show truthful results
stories.userValue: Verify reachability before saving without persisting drafts. These are proposed delivery acceptance criteria, to be validated by this Story’s build; they do not assert existing production support. Proposed delivery dependency rationale: [[c19]].

functionalRequirements.statement: Required outcome: Test the current draft safely and show truthful results.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A current draft with retained or replacement credentials
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: The test uses the same merged configuration as Save, writes no draft config or secrets, sanitizes errors, shows duration, and never claims schema completeness

acceptanceCriteria.when: the draft changes, repository switches, or form closes
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Late results are ignored; repeated tests are disabled while pending, a 10-second timeout allows retry, and transient resources are released

stories.title: Use temporary connections within a workbench session
stories.userValue: Analyze one-off files or other supported sources without leaving saved connections. These are proposed delivery acceptance criteria, to be validated by this Story’s build; they do not assert existing production support. Proposed delivery dependency rationale: [[c20]].

functionalRequirements.statement: Required outcome: Use temporary connections within a workbench session.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A repository and active workbench session
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user selects Temporary session and adds a source
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Config and credentials stay only in memory; duplicates across visible scopes fail; analysis in this session resolves it while other sessions cannot

acceptanceCriteria.when: the panel closes, repository switches, workbench session ends, or daemon restarts
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Panel closure and repository switching retain them; session end or daemon restart expires configs, secrets and resources; lifetime is explained before adding

stories.title: Discard temporary and delete saved connections safely
stories.userValue: Clean up unused registrations without deleting data. These are proposed delivery acceptance criteria, to be validated by this Story’s build; they do not assert existing production support. Proposed delivery dependency rationale: [[c21]].

functionalRequirements.statement: Required outcome: Discard temporary and delete saved connections safely.

acceptanceCriteria.when: the user selects Delete or Discard
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Confirmation identifies ID and scope and protects source data; cancel preserves it; successful revision-checked removal removes only registration and owned credentials and releases idle resources

acceptanceCriteria.given: A connection is busy, stale, or removal fails or has an uncertain response
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Busy/stale failures retain the row with retry guidance; uncertain outcomes reconcile idempotently and no new analysis resolves a successfully removed connection

stories.title: Manage and filter connections from Settings in both VS Code clients
stories.userValue: Find and maintain connections in the editor. These are proposed delivery acceptance criteria, to be validated by this Story’s build; they do not assert existing production support. Proposed delivery dependency rationale: [[c22]].

functionalRequirements.statement: Required outcome: Manage and filter connections from Settings in both VS Code clients.

acceptanceCriteria.given: The user searches insrc connections in Settings
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: The themed editor retains the selected registered repository; multi-root selection is explicit, all daemon-supported drivers are offered, and existing palette/editor entry points share behavior

acceptanceCriteria.when: the user lists, filters, adds or edits connections
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: All/Saved/Temporary filters show scope badges and matching counts; loading, empty registry, empty filter, failed read and offline states differ; new adds become visible and dirty form navigation offers discard/cancel

acceptanceCriteria.given: Dark/light themes, keyboard users, or mixed client/daemon versions
acceptanceCriteria.then: Required result: Controls have labels and visible focus, errors retain drafts, secrets stay masked, and explicit compatibility behavior is verified in extension and IDE-fork integration

requirements.statement: Required outcome: Users can manage all daemon-supported drivers across saved and temporary lifetimes with truthful outcomes and protected credentials.
Required outcome: Connections remain repository scoped, and temporary connections are visible only within their originating workbench session.
Required outcome: Manage saved endpoints and credentials without losing configuration.
Required outcome: Test the current draft safely and show truthful results.
Required outcome: Use temporary connections within a workbench session.
Required outcome: Discard temporary and delete saved connections safely.
Required outcome: Manage and filter connections from Settings in both VS Code clients.
